studies.label: Lab experiment: Product Improvement Task with vs. without ChatGPT

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 11, Participants and Table 1 headers; analyzed arm counts only
counts_source.quote: The control group for the present study contained 68 university students and the experimental group contained 77 participants

arms.name: Experimental (ChatGPT)
arms.description: Solved the Product Improvement Task with ChatGPT-3.5 (Plus) open in a second browser tab, following a short description with example prompts and responses. Task instructions explicitly referred to ChatGPT assistance. Participants also answered additional self-efficacy questions (PDF pp. 10, 13).

arms.name: Control (no ChatGPT)
arms.description: Solved the same Product Improvement Task in a single browser tab without ChatGPT. Both conditions could access additional browser tools, but no participant did so (PDF p. 10).

studies.task: Generate three original and useful improvements to an ordinary stuffed bunny to help Mattel achieve higher sales than the Lego Group (PDF pp. 12-13).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-3.5 (Plus)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 10, Experimental Procedure; model/product release year is not stated.

preregistration.where: osf.io/q6wtu (PDF p. 9); hypotheses on PDF pp. 8-9. The OSF API and OSF page could not be retrieved because network access was denied.

The paper does not explain how ratings or individual ideas were combined into a participant score.

estimates.outcome: Originality change from baseline UUT to experimental PIT (group-by-task interaction)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Expert-rated originality in the UUT baseline and PIT experimental task; Figure 1 labels the outcome "Originality (z-scores)" (PDF p. 17). UUT answers were rated by two trained experts, blind to condition, from 1 (no originality) to 5 (high originality), and the two expert judgments were averaged (PDF p. 12). PIT uses the scale and procedures on PDF p. 13 and the rubric in Appendix 1, PDF p. 40. The z-score reference distribution is not stated.

paper_effect.standardizer: Reported as partial eta squared (eta-squared with subscript p); the paper does not state the denominator formula. The eta2 code denotes that printed partial measure here.

estimates.notes: Full-sample randomized-group comparison of change between the unassisted baseline UUT and the experimental PIT. The paper describes this as the significant interaction term and reports improvement with ChatGPT. Both groups always completed UUT before PIT (PDF p. 10); random assignment was between participants, so within_person is null. This is another specification of the originality treatment effect, not an independent sample. The surrounding analysis uses prior ChatGPT experience as a covariate, but the repeated-measures model is not fully specified. Figure 1 plots z-score means and 95% CI bars without numeric labels; arm levels, change scores, SEs, and interval limits remain null. The analysis is at participant level, as indicated by the independent-samples design and reported test degrees of freedom; the precise aggregation of ideas and raters is not specified. Arm counts are the printed analyzed counts on PDF p. 11. The PDF prints no combined participant total, so n_total is null. Sessions were separated by condition; no session adjustment is reported.

open_items: The PDF prints only the arm counts, not a combined total. Study n_analyzed and estimate n_total are null rather than sums. Numbers assigned before the experiment, the randomization mechanism, and possible nonattendance are not reported; all randomized-count fields remain null. The statement that no participants were excluded (PDF p. 10) refers to participants who completed the experiment.

The PIT scoring description does not explain how the two experts’ ratings or a participant’s three solutions were aggregated, or explicitly identify the PIT raters. Participant-level unit and SD level follow the reported participant comparison; identities and averaging are stated only for UUT (PDF pp. 12-13).

No primary outcome is identified among the preregistered quality, elaboration, and originality hypotheses. The preregistration could not be checked: requests to the OSF registration API and OSF page both failed with network access denied. preregistered_primary remains not_stated.

Conditions ran in separate sessions with a maximum of five participants at a time (PDF p. 10). The number and scheduling of sessions are not reported, and no session-clustered uncertainty is given. Individual random assignment is explicitly stated.

Table 2 does not define the SD denominator of d. ANCOVA and interaction results give F and partial eta squared but no adjusted means, signed differences, SDs, SEs, or numeric confidence intervals. Figure 1 shows only plotted z-score means and confidence bars.
The exact model/product name is ChatGPT-3.5 (Plus), but its release year is not stated in this PDF; ai_tool.year is null.
The saved document is an accepted manuscript, not the journal copy of record. The retrieval and citation records identify a later journal version, which was not used in this extraction.
notes: Extracted by A on 2026-10-10. The entire markdown was read in order, including references and Appendix 1. All PDF pages cited here were text-extracted with PyMuPDF; Figure 1 was also inspected as a rendered page. The study contains one randomized comparison. The unadjusted, ANCOVA, and group-by-task records are overlapping specifications, not independent samples. The paper describes ANCOVAs adjusted for pre-experiment ChatGPT experience as its hypothesis-testing analysis (PDF p. 16); that is its main specification when resolving a specification tie under codebook section 8. No primary outcome is confirmed, and no new primary designation is inferred from the blocked preregistration. Country is inferred from the laboratory being at the first author’s institution (PDF p. 9) and that institution’s Prague, Czech Republic address (PDF p. 1), consistent with the reconciled form. The treatment includes a ChatGPT introduction and additional self-efficacy questions (PDF pp. 10, 13). No across_people or after_ai outcomes are reported. All numeric statistics are transcribed without effect-size, count, SE, or interval calculations; source quotes preserve printed precision.
